findings.title: Null pointer dereference when destinationCalendar is empty or undefined
findings.body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array `[]`, the destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined`. The subsequent access `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` on line 119 will throw a TypeError at runtime. This crashes the entire booking creation flow for any event using Google Meet location where no destination calendar is configured. A null-check like `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` is needed.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback logic is dead code — find condition can never match
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, the fallback branch `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is reached only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Since the find condition compares `cal.externalId` against the same falsy `externalCalendarId`, it will never match any calendar. This means `selectedCalendar` will be `undefined`, and `calendar.events.update` will be called with `calendarId: undefined`, likely causing a Google API error. The same issue exists in `deleteEvent` at line 317. The original code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` which was correct.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback logic is dead code — same issue as updateEvent
findings.body: In `deleteEvent`, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, making the find condition impossible to satisfy. The result is `calendarId` being `undefined`, which then falls through to `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`. While this doesn't crash (due to the ternary on line 322), it silently deletes from the wrong calendar if the event was on a non-primary calendar and `externalCalendarId` wasn't passed.

findings.title: updateEvent called with potentially undefined credential
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup also fails (e.g., credential was deleted), the variable `credential` remains `undefined`. The code then calls `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` with `undefined` as the credential. The `updateEvent` function in CalendarManager.ts accesses `credential.type` and `credential.appName`, which will throw a TypeError. A guard should skip or handle the case where credential is not found.

findings.title: loadUsers error handling swallows specific error messages and changes behavior
findings.body: The refactored `loadUsers` wraps all errors in a try-catch that throws `HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: 'Unable to load users' })` for non-HttpError/non-Prisma errors. This means the specific error 'dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty' thrown on line 727 is caught and replaced with a generic 500 message, losing diagnostic information. Additionally, the original code did not have this try-catch, so errors that previously propagated naturally are now wrapped differently, potentially changing how callers handle failures.

findings.title: organization.slug removed from user select may break downstream code
findings.body: The `loadUsers` refactoring removed `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the Prisma select for users when `eventTypeId` is falsy (dynamic booking path). If any downstream code in the booking flow accesses `user.organization?.slug` (e.g., for URL construction or organization-aware logic), it will now get `undefined` instead of the actual slug, potentially breaking organization-related features for dynamic bookings.

findings.title: createAllCalendarEvents silently skips events when credential not found
findings.body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination calendar has a `credentialId` but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup returns null (e.g., credential was deleted), the code silently skips creating the calendar event for that host. No error is logged or surfaced. For collective events, this means a host could silently not receive a calendar invitation with no indication of failure to the organizer or the affected host.

findings.title: Inconsistent destinationCalendar expectations between webhook test cases
findings.body: The BOOKING_CREATED test expects `destinationCalendar: null` (line 119) while BOOKING_REJECTED expects `destinationCalendar: []` (line 249). This inconsistency suggests that the BOOKING_CREATED webhook payload path hasn't been updated to use the new array format, or the test isn't reflecting the actual behavior. If the type is now `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, both paths should produce consistent output (either both `[]` or both `null` when no calendar is set).

findings.title: Calendar interface createEvent signature change is a breaking contract for implementations
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface now requires `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`, but LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and BaseCalendarService (CalDAV) still declare `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` without the `credentialId` parameter. While TypeScript allows this (fewer params are assignable), these implementations cannot use `credentialId` to select the correct calendar from the array for collective events. This means multi-host collective events will only create calendar events on the first host's calendar for Lark, Office365, and CalDAV integrations, defeating the purpose of this PR for those providers.

findings.title: Sequential DB queries inside loop for credential lookup in createAllCalendarEvents
findings.body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, for each destination calendar in the array, if the credential isn't found in memory, a `prisma.credential.findUnique` query is made sequentially inside the for-loop. For collective events with many hosts, this results in N sequential database queries. These could be batched into a single `findMany` query with an `id: { in: [...] }` filter before the loop to reduce latency.
